title: Surjectivity on first Tor for a quotient after change of rings
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal, $J=IA\subseteq A$ the ideal generated by the image of $I$, $M$ an $R$-module, and $N=M\otimes_RA$ its base change to $A$. Choose a free $R$-resolution $F_\bullet\to M$ and a free $A$-resolution $G_\bullet\to N$ with a chain map $F_\bullet\otimes_RA\to G_\bullet$ lifting the identity of $N$. The induced map on first homology $H_1(F_\bullet\otimes_R(A/J))\to H_1(G_\bullet\otimes_A(A/J))$, namely the change-of-rings map $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(M,A/J)\to\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(N,A/J)$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], is surjective.

proof.text: Put E = extendScalars(f), K = E(F), and ε = E(F.π₀). The augmentation ε is epi and K₁ → K₀ → E(M) is exact: F.exact₀ and E being a left adjoint give preservation of the cokernel by ShortComplex.Exact.map_of_epi_of_preservesCokernel. This is the categorical form of tensor right exactness [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]. The statement already uses K tensor A/J, so no further tensor cancellation is required.

proof.text: The fully proved private helper epi_homology_one_of_right_exact applies to any right-exact augmented complex K mapping to a projective resolution G of the same object, and any additive functor T. Lift G.π₀ through ε using projectivity of G₀ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], obtaining b₀ : G₀ → K₀ with b₀ ≫ ε = G.π₀. Since d_G ≫ b₀ ≫ ε = 0, exactness at K₀ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] and projectivity of G₁ give b₁ : G₁ → K₁ with b₁ ≫ d_K = d_G ≫ b₀. Mathlib Projective.factorThru and ShortComplex.Exact.liftFromProjective construct these maps.

proof.text: The augmentation condition makes (b₀ ≫ φ₀ - 1) ≫ G.π₀ = 0. Exactness at G₀ and projectivity of G₀ give s₀ : G₀ → G₁ with s₀ ≫ d_G = b₀ ≫ φ₀ - 1. The chain map identity and the equation for b₁ imply (b₁ ≫ φ₁ - 1 - d_G ≫ s₀) ≫ d_G = 0. Exactness at G₁ and projectivity of G₁ give s₁ : G₁ → G₂ with s₁ ≫ d_G = b₁ ≫ φ₁ - 1 - d_G ≫ s₀. This is a partial homotopy right inverse; no map b₂ or replacement resolution is needed.

proof.text: Apply the additive functor T = tensoringRight(A/J). The equation for b₁ constructs z from cycles of T(G) to cycles of T(K). The homotopy equations give z ≫ cyclesMap(Tφ) = 1 + (iCycles ≫ T(s₁)) ≫ toCycles₂₁: the term through d_G vanishes on cycles. Compose with homologyπ; the boundary term vanishes by HomologicalComplex.toCycles_comp_homologyπ, and naturality gives (z ≫ homologyπ) ≫ homologyMap(Tφ) = homologyπ of T(G). This last projection is epi, so epi_of_epi makes homologyMap(Tφ) epi. ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective proves the unchanged conclusion. The freeness assumptions are retained but unnecessary; projectivity comes directly from ProjectiveResolution.
